svg.text: Everything on this page happened, or was first reported, on Wednesday 18 November 2026.
Xi welcomes Trump on the tarmac in
The APEC summit opened as Air Force One landed at Shenzhen Baoan. Xi
Jinping greeted President Trump personally on the tarmac — the first US
president to visit the city. A state banquet followed, with Putin seated
between the two leaders. Three-way talks on trade, Ukraine and arms
Bahrain and Kuwait intercept Iran drone
Iran launched waves of Shahed drones and Fateh ballistic missiles at US
Patriot radar sites in Bahrain and at an air-defence base near Kuwait City.
Both countries said their interceptors knocked down the bulk of the attack.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard called it retaliation for Tuesday's US airstrike
Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth
NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory confirmed that Voyager 1, launched in 1977,
crossed the milestone of 25.9 billion kilometres — exactly one light-day — from
Earth at 03:14 UTC. The probe remains operational, returning plasma-wave and
logistics. Air Force Command said 126 of 141 Shahed
October FOMC minutes show broad concern over
release. Rate futures price 72% chance of a
The India Met Department raised red alerts for
Odisha as Cyclone Akvan, a Category 2 storm, was
tracking NNE at 12 knots. Landfall expected Friday.
Amnesty International said at least 37 civilians were
killed in Rapid Support Forces drone attacks on the
city's market and hospital on Tuesday.
The European Commission's draft would front-load

ONS said CPI rose to 3.6% in October, up from 2.6% in
September. Services inflation hit 5.9%. The Bank of
England now seen on hold through February.
IDF armoured units advanced along the main Salah
ad-Din Road toward the Nuseirat camp. Hospitals in
central Gaza reported severe fuel shortages.
House Democrats voted 251–11 to nominate Hakeem
Jeffries as Speaker for the new Congress.

GTA VI goes on sale after a
Rockstar's most anticipated game launched on PS5
and Xbox Series X globally. It broke Steam's
concurrent-player record within two hours of going
Tens of thousands of workers walked off the job in
Dhaka and Chittagong over unpaid October wages.
Factory owners confirmed at least 55 plants closed.
